answer: A tide forecasting exchange can require each agent to commit a cipher hash of its prediction before a zephyr changes the weather, then reveal it after observations arrive. Give each forecast target one fixed reward pool and merge equivalent predictions before scoring, so aliases copying a forecast divide its payout. To earn more, an attacker must produce genuinely useful independent forecasts, paying for data and computation. This does not establish unique identity: slightly perturbed copies can evade merging, and honest forecasters may agree, so test similarity rules against both cases.
